verdict.rationale: Daytona's own docs describe sandboxes as isolated runtime environments for running code. Each sandbox gets a dedicated kernel, filesystem, network stack and allocated resources, VM-backed sandboxes are available, and a per-sandbox firewall explicitly prevents untrusted code from exfiltrating data; the product positions itself as secure infrastructure for running AI-generated code. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that the isolation holds, and deeper documentation of the isolation technology and threat model (e.g., escape protections).

support.subject: As a developer, I can execute untrusted, AI-generated code without risking my own infrastructure

citations.quote: Each sandbox runs in isolation, giving it a dedicated kernel, filesystem, network stack, and allocated vCPU, RAM, and disk.
Each sandbox runs behind a firewall that restricts which external IP addresses and domains it can reach, preventing untrusted code from exfiltrating data or contacting arbitrary hosts.
Sandboxes are isolated runtime environments you can manage programmatically to run code.
Daytona is a secure and elastic infrastructure for running AI-generated code.
Daytona also provides VM sandboxes with a dedicated Linux VM or Windows operating system
